headline: Who owns the water: the MMR's allocation ledger
intro: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region has no water utility: nine city corporations drink from a shared set of dams under a patchwork of quotas, agreements and beneficiary tables. This ledger shows, for every arrangement, what the paper promises, what the pipe actually delivers, and how solid the paper is - a view no institution publishes.
unit_note: All Mumbai figures are in MLD (million litres per day). Receipts carry the year they were reported.

authorities.name: STEM Water Distribution & Infrastructure Co.
authorities.role: A water company owned jointly by the three cities it serves. It pumps water from the Ulhas river at Shahad (near Kalyan), treats it, and pipes it to Thane, Mira-Bhayandar and Bhiwandi.
authorities.capacity: 285 MLD sanctioned quota (313.5 MLD penalty-free lift ceiling)
authorities.committed: ~330 MLD promised across Thane, Mira-Bhayandar and Bhiwandi
authorities.tension: Oversubscribed on its own paper: STEM's board minutes put the sanctioned quota at 285 MLD, while the promises across Thane, Mira-Bhayandar and Bhiwandi sum to ~330 - the structural cause of the perennial three-way quota fights.

authorities.name: MIDC (Barvi dam)
authorities.role: Maharashtra's industrial-estates agency. It built the Barvi dam to supply factories - but the drinking water of four cities (Thane, Mira-Bhayandar, Ulhasnagar, Kalyan-Dombivli) now depends on buying Barvi water from it.
authorities.capacity: Barvi supplies ~460 MLD to municipal bodies (of its larger yield)
authorities.tension: A factory-water agency is the tap for ~2 million people, and it does not publish the rules for who gets how much - every quota on this page had to be reconstructed from press reports.

authorities.name: MMRDA (Surya regional scheme)
authorities.role: The region's planning and infrastructure authority. It built the new 403 MLD Surya scheme in Palghar and decides which cities receive it: Vasai-Virar (flowing since 2023) and Mira-Bhayandar (pipeline under construction).
authorities.capacity: 403 MLD (GoM allocated 146.33 Mm3/yr from Surya dam via WRD)
authorities.committed: VVCMC (Phase 1, flowing) + MBMC (Phase 2, 218 MLD, in progress)
authorities.tension: The only authority here that publishes who gets how much - which is why the Surya rows are the best-documented entitlements in the region.

authorities.name: CIDCO (Hetawane system)
authorities.role: The state corporation that built Navi Mumbai as a planned city. It owns the Hetawane dam supply system and delivers most of Panvel's water to the townships it built there.
authorities.committed: ~179 MLD to Panvel's nodes (plus Morbe water for Kamothe via NMMC)
authorities.tension: Panvel's own environmental report shows the dependency: about 179 of its 220 MLD arrives through CIDCO - an authority the elected corporation does not control.

authorities.name: MWRRA (tariff regulator)
authorities.role: The state's water-price regulator. It sets the official rate at which bulk water changes hands between dams, authorities and cities.
authorities.tension: Municipal domestic bulk water is priced at Rs 0.55 per cubic metre (2022 order) - roughly a twentieth of a rupee per bucket. A new control period began 1 July 2026 (order dated 18 June 2026), raising bulk tariffs 10% in 2027-28 and 20% in 2028-29. The regulator's own Register of Non-Irrigation Entitlements page is literally marked 'Under Construction'.

events.title: Pinjal reallocated from Vasai-Virar to BMC
events.note: The Pinjal source, originally earmarked for Vasai-Virar, was moved to Greater Mumbai - the clearest documented case of the core city's claims overriding the periphery's. Vasai-Virar waited until 2023 (Surya) for a major source of its own, and today runs the region's lowest per-capita supply (~70 LPCD).

futures.status: Planned (KIDC, MMRDA-funded); long delayed by forest and displacement disputes

Planned/stalled - the source taken from Vasai-Virar in 1999 has still not been built

gaps: STEM's per-city split (Thane ~150, Bhiwandi ~94) is still press-reconstructed - its tariff page names the buyers but no quantities; only the MBMC leg (86) is officially published, by MBMC itself.
MIDC publishes buyer lists and rates but no quantities; Ulhasnagar's 112 sanction and KDMC's ~50 rest on a 2011 academic record and press.

MWRRA's Register of Non-Irrigation Entitlements - the page that should hold every quota on this ledger - is marked 'Under Construction'; the 2026-29 tariff order confirms quantities live in unpublished supplier-corporation agreements.

The Barvi water-sharing GR (UDD, 18 Sep 2017) is identified by number - it apportions the dam-raise among six named bodies 'per the equitable principle of water use' - but the PDF itself is not retrievable online.
BMC's 90 MLD bulk sale to Thane has no public instrument; an archived reference suggests a GoM permission to draw against BMC's Bhatsa allotment.
No arrangement has a public receipt time-series - only the Surya scheme (MMRDA) and the dams themselves (Pravah) are tracked.
